title: Why the Giant Dundee Stirling Failed

segments.text: Did a massive Stirling engine ever power a foundry?
In the early 1840s James Stirling installed a large hot‑air engine in Dundee, proving the design could deliver industrial‑scale power.
The machine ran briefly, but components exposed to scorching temperatures cracked, warped and failed repeatedly.
Those high‑temperature failures led owners to replace it with a conventional steam engine.
After the setback, smaller hot‑air engines appeared from the 1860s, pumping water and supplying air to church organs.
Their simple operation made them attractive where steam engines required constant supervision, keeping the Stirling alive
